Title: AI Agents for Restaurants in Miami | Stanzi Studio

AI automation agency · Miami

# Five AI agents for restaurants. Every one answers to the owner.

Stanzi Studio is a Miami AI automation agency for restaurants, caterers and venues. We build AI agents that answer catering inquiries, reply to reviews, read vendor invoices and email the owner yesterday's numbers by 7am. Each one works inside rules you approve. Money, contracts, angry guests and anything legal always go to you. Setup takes about ten days.

We don't advise. We operate.

What the agents do

## Five agents, one job each.

They started as fixes for restaurants we run ourselves. Order one, or stack a few. Every price below is fixed and published on our menu.

01

### Catering inquiry desk

$1,500 + $500/mo · The Pass · setup + monthly

Every catering inquiry answered in minutes, and followed up until it books.

It replies from your own email address, day or night, in English or Spanish. It asks for the date, the headcount and the budget, drafts the quote from your price list and sends it to you to approve. Leads that go quiet get a follow-up. Booked events land on your calendar.

How the catering desk works

02

### Review desk

$750 + $200/mo · Front of House · per location

Every review answered. The bad ones go to a person.

Four- and five-star reviews get a reply in your voice and in the guest's language, posted on their own. Anything at three stars or under never posts by itself. It goes to that location's manager with a draft reply, the same day.

03

### Morning numbers

$2,500 + $400/mo · The Close · per location

Yesterday's P&L in your inbox by 7am.

It pulls sales from Square or Toast every night, reads vendor invoices from a photo and lays out labor. You get one page each morning with yesterday and month to date, plus an alert when food or labor cost runs hot. It lives in a Google Sheet you own.

04

### Invoice desk

$5,000 + $500/mo · The Walk-In · build + per location

Every vendor invoice, read line by line.

Vendors email one address, and your team texts a photo of anything on paper. Every line gets filed by item, so you can see what chicken or boxes cost you this week and every week before it. Once a month it checks each vendor's statement. Price changes and missing credits come to you with the invoice attached. Text it a question and it answers from your own invoices.

05

### Built to order

From $2,500 · Off the Menu · quoted after a 15-min call

One agent for the job that eats your week.

A support inbox that answers the routine questions and passes the rest to a person. A sales inbox that replies to new leads and books the call on your calendar. Prep lists built from your sales. Tell us the job on a 15-minute call. We quote it fixed, build it in ten days and hand it over documented.

Who approves what

## Two lists decide what an agent can do alone.

Before anything goes live, we write the rules down in plain English and you approve them along with the copy. The agent works inside them. Everything else comes to you.

The agent handles

- First replies. Any hour, in English or Spanish, from your own address.

- The questions a quote needs. Date, headcount and budget, asked up front.

- Follow-ups. Every lead that goes quiet gets a nudge.

- Good reviews. Four and five stars get a reply, posted on its own.

- The paperwork. Invoices filed, statements checked, the 7am numbers sent.

Always comes to you

- Quotes and prices. Drafted for you, sent only after you approve them.

- Money. Refunds, discounts, deposits and payment terms.

- Contracts. An agent never signs, accepts or changes one.

- Angry guests. Complaints and reviews at three stars or under go to a person, the same day.

- Anything legal. A lawyer, a reporter or a health complaint goes straight to the owner.

What it costs

What this does not include

## Five things we don't sell.

- A chatbot that guesses. Answers come from your menu, your price list and the rules you approved. If it doesn't know, it asks you.

- Ad spend. We don't run or mark up your ads.

- A new website. We work inside the site and the inbox you already have.

- New software for your staff to learn. Everything lands in email, Google Sheets or the tools you already use.

The exit

## In plain English, and easy to leave.

- You own every account. Your inbox, your Google, your sheets. We get admin access, never ownership.

- You keep everything we built. If you cancel, the sheets, the rules and the pages stay yours.

- 30 days' notice. No cancellation fee and no awkward call.

Questions

## Nine things owners ask first.

### What does an AI agent actually do in a restaurant?

One job, start to finish, inside rules you set. Ours answer catering inquiries, reply to reviews, file vendor invoices and send the morning numbers. They do the typing and the chasing. Anything with money, a contract or an upset guest comes to you.

### How much do AI agents for restaurants cost?

Our prices are fixed and published. The review desk is $750 to set up and $200 a month per location. The catering inquiry desk is $1,500 plus $500 a month. Full Service for a whole group is $7,500 plus $2,000 a month. Custom builds start at $2,500.

### Will an agent send a quote or a price without me?

No. Quotes are drafted from your price list and wait for your approval. Refunds, discounts, deposits and contracts always go to you.

### How long does setup take?

About ten days, and about an hour of your time. The catering desk comes with a promise: live in 14 days or your first month is free.

### Which systems does it work with?

Square and Toast for sales, your own email address for inquiries, and Google Sheets for anything you want to read. The invoice desk runs next to MarginEdge or xtraCHEF, or on its own.

### Does it reply in Spanish?

Yes. Replies go out in English or Spanish, matching the person who wrote in.

### Do you only work with Miami restaurants?

We're based in Miami and work across Miami-Dade, Broward and the rest of South Florida. We take on restaurants elsewhere in the US as well.

### How do I leave?

Give 30 days' notice. There's no cancellation fee, and everything we built stays yours: the accounts, the sheets and the rules.

### Who builds it?

A small Miami team that runs the same systems in our own restaurants and built Opstable, our restaurant workforce software. You get one person to text, not a ticket queue.

Title: Catering Inquiry Automation for Caterers | Stanzi Studio

Catering inquiry automation · For caterers, restaurants and venues

# One desk answers every catering inquiry in minutes.

Catering inquiry automation is an AI agent that answers every catering lead from your own inbox within minutes. It asks for the date, headcount and budget, drafts the quote from your price list for you to approve, follows up on quiet leads and puts booked events on your calendar. Stanzi Studio sets it up in about ten days.

We don't advise. We operate.

The problem

## One rule of catering: the job goes to whoever answers first.

Someone planning an office lunch or a rehearsal dinner sends the same request to several places. They book whoever comes back first with real answers. At our own restaurant, the leads we closed were the ones that got a real reply the same day.

A form that sits in a shared inbox over the weekend is a job handed to someone else.

How it works

## Five steps from inquiry to calendar.

- 01Reply in minutes. From your own email address, in English or Spanish, at 11pm on a Sunday the same as at noon on a Tuesday.

- 02Ask what the quote needs. Date, headcount and budget up front, plus anything your prices depend on, like a delivery address or pickup.

- 03Draft the quote from your price list. Your packages, your per-person prices, your minimums. If a request doesn't fit the list, the desk doesn't guess. It holds the lead for you.

- 04Wait for your approval. The draft comes to you first. Change what you want, approve it, and it goes out.

- 05Follow up, then book. Leads that go quiet get a follow-up. When a job books, it lands on your calendar.

What comes to you

## Four kinds of inquiry always come to you.

The desk does the typing and the chasing. Judgment calls stay with the owner.

- Every quote. Drafted for you and sent only after you approve it.

- Anything off your price list. A custom menu, a date you're closed, or a headcount above the limit you set.

- Money. Deposits, refunds, discounts and payment terms.

- Complaints, contracts and anything legal. An unhappy client, a contract to sign, or anyone mentioning a lawyer or the press.

Setup

## Three things you give us on day one.

- 01Your catering price list. A PDF is fine. We turn it into rules the desk can read, and you check them before anything goes live.

- 02Access to the inbox your inquiries land in. You give us a login and take it back whenever you like. Your website and your form stay where they are.

- 03Your rules. How much notice you need, the biggest event you'll take without a call, where you deliver, and what you always want to see first.

What it costs

## $1,500 to set up. $500 a month.

That's The Pass on our menu. After setup it's month to month, with 30 days' notice to leave. It's live in 14 days or your first month is free.

- $3,000 setupWith Full House. Catering search pages that bring in more inquiries for the desk to answer. Setup for both is $3,000.

- $7,500 + $2,000/moFull Service. For dedicated caterers, event venues and groups with three or more locations. The catering pipeline runs across every location, with one screen that shows all of it.

Where it comes from

## Built for our own restaurant's catering first.

We operate a two-location pizzeria in Miami. Its catering inquiries get a reply drafted within hours, quiet leads get a nudge and paid jobs land on the calendar on their own. Monthly catering sales there grew more than 1,800% from June to September 2026. Read the case study.

One honest note from that work: the desk doesn't create demand. Search pages did most of that lift. If nobody finds you, there's nothing to answer, which is why the desk pairs well with Full House.

What this does not include

## Four things the desk won't do.

- Take payment. Deposits and invoices stay with you and your POS.

- Make up a dish or a price. It only quotes what's on your list.

- Replace your website or your form. It works from the inbox you already have.

- Lock you in. Setup is paid once. Monthly is month to month.

The exit

## In plain English, and easy to leave.

- You own the inbox and the calendar. We get access, never ownership.

- You keep the rules we wrote. Your price list, in a form any person or tool can use.

- 30 days' notice. No cancellation fee and no awkward call.

Questions

## Seven things caterers ask first.

### What is catering inquiry automation?

An agent that handles the first part of every catering lead for you: the reply, the questions, the draft quote and the follow-up. You approve the quote. It does the typing and the chasing.

### Will it send a quote without my approval?

No. Every quote and price comes to you first. Nothing with a dollar sign goes out until you approve it.

### Can it quote from my own price list?

Yes. We load your packages, per-person prices and minimums. If a request doesn't fit the list, the desk holds it for you instead of guessing.

### Does it work for caterers and event venues, or only restaurants?

Both. Any business that gets catering inquiries by email or web form can use it. Full Service is built for dedicated caterers, event venues and groups with three or more locations.

### Does it answer in Spanish?

Yes. It replies in English or Spanish, matching the person who wrote in.

### How much does catering inquiry automation cost?

$1,500 to set up and $500 a month. Add Full House catering search pages and setup is $3,000 for both.

### How fast can it go live?

About ten days, and about an hour of your time. If it isn't live in 14 days, your first month is free.

Become a Client

## One 15-minute call, then a fixed price.

Bring your catering price list. You'll leave the call with a fixed price and a date the desk goes live. For the rest of what we build for restaurants, see AI agents for restaurants.

Become a Client

Or email franco@stanzistudio.com · See the menu and prices · Based in Miami. Built on systems.

We operate two pizzerias in Miami. The systems below started there. They bring in the catering inquiries, answer the reviews and close out the day's numbers. Nothing on this page was built for a pitch.

The Menu

## Seven plates and one tasting menu.

Order one or stack a few. Every price is fixed and setup takes about ten days. After that it's month to month.

House plates

01

### Full House

$1,500 + $750/mo · Setup + monthly

Catering search. When someone near you searches "catering", you show up.

Most restaurants have one catering page with a PDF on it, and Google can't read a PDF. We build the pages that rank: one per event type and one per neighborhood you deliver to, with your menu in real text.

- 6–8 catering pages: weddings, offices, parties, neighborhoods

- Catering menu rebuilt as text Google can read

- Structured data so Google and AI assistants know what you cater

- Google Business Profile catering cleanup

- An inquiry form that asks the headcount

- 2 new pages a month and a monthly search report

Most ordered

Daily P&L. Yesterday's numbers in your inbox by 7am.

- Sales pulled from Square or Toast nightly

Review replies. Every review answered, and the bad ones escalated.

AI search. When someone asks ChatGPT or Google "best Cuban in Miami," your name comes up.

We make sure it has what it needs to name you: clear facts about your restaurant, answers to the questions guests ask, and the same details everywhere it looks. Every month we ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity the same 20 questions and show you who they recommend.

- Business and FAQ markup AI assistants can read

- Answer-first FAQ pages in English and Spanish

It asks for the date, the headcount and the budget, then follows up with the ones that go quiet. Quotes and prices never go out on their own. They come to you to approve first, and every booked event lands on your calendar.

$5,000 + $500/mo · Build + per location

Your vendor invoices, built into one system. Every delivery, every line, every price.

We build you a receiving desk. Every vendor emails invoices to one address, and your team texts a photo of anything on paper. Each invoice is read line by line and filed by item, so you can see what chicken, cheese and boxes cost you this week and every week before it. Once a month it is matched to each vendor's statement, and any price change or missing credit comes to you with the invoice attached. Text it a question and it answers from your own invoices. It runs next to MarginEdge or xtraCHEF, or on its own.

- One invoice address for every vendor

- Paper invoices sent as a text photo

- Every line saved: item, quantity, unit price

- Matched to vendor statements every month

- Price changes and missing credits flagged, invoice attached

- Ask it by text, it answers from your invoices

Title: Restaurant Catering SEO Case Study, Miami, Stanzi Studio

Case study · Stanzione, Miami

# Catering up more than 1,800% in four months.

Stanzione is a two-location Neapolitan pizzeria in downtown Miami and Citadel. It's also our own restaurant. From June to September 2026, monthly catering sales grew more than 1,800%. Here's exactly what we built, in order, with the results.

We don't advise. We operate.

The numbers

## Four months of catering sales, against June.

Month (2026) | Change vs. June

June | Baseline

July | −21%

August | +504%

September | +1,838%

Source: the restaurant's catering POS. July was flat. The first pages went live on July 7, and Google takes weeks to start sending traffic to new pages. Search did most of the work. A small paid-social test ran alongside it, and those leads are inside these numbers.

What we built

## Five changes, in the order we made them.

- Jun 11An audit. We searched the way a customer would. "Pizza catering Miami" landed on the wrong page, and searches for weddings, offices and corporate events didn't land on us at all.

- Jul 7Catering pages that match real searches. One hub page, plus separate pages for live pizza catering, weddings, corporate events and office lunches. Each page answers the questions people actually type.

- Jul–AugOne page per neighborhood we deliver to. Brickell, Wynwood, Miami Beach, Coral Gables, Coconut Grove, Edgewater, Design District and Downtown. All live by August 10.

- AugStructured data on every catering page. Restaurant and location markup plus 50+ FAQ answers, so Google and AI assistants can read exactly what we cater, where, and for how many.

- Sep–OctThe follow-through. Every inquiry gets a reply drafted within hours, quiet leads get a nudge, paid jobs land on the calendar automatically, and 4- and 5-star Google reviews get answered automatically.

What Google shows

## Fifteen pages, 11,810 searches, 164 clicks.

11,810

Times our 15 catering pages appeared in Google search, July to September.

Google Search Console

164

Clicks to those pages in the same quarter. These are people looking for catering, not for dinner.

Google Search Console

#3.8

Average position for "mobile pizza oven catering miami". That's page one, without paid ads.

Google Search Console · Jul–Sep 2026

What didn't work

## One thing we'd skip next time.

- An automated lead engine on its own. We built one, and by itself it didn't move catering. The search pages did. Get found first, then automate the follow-up.

What carries over

## Three things work for any restaurant that caters.

- 01Get found for the search, not the brand. People search "catering" plus an event or a neighborhood. If no page answers that, the order goes to whoever has one.

- 02Make the page readable by machines. Structured data and plain answers are how Google and AI assistants decide who to show.

- 03Answer fast. The leads we closed were the ones that got a real reply the same day.
